1) the preparation and characterization of subfractions from mouse liver, with special emphasis to their suitability for use as a tool in studies of epoxides hydrolases, was studied; 2) it was found that 13,3 00 0 gav for 6 0 min (i.e., more extensive force than 1 0 5,000 gav, 1 h) was necessary to get membrane-free cytosol; and 3

the subcellular distributions of the different enzyme markers in mouse liver closely resemble those reported in the literature for rat liver, that starvation has no significant effect on epoxide hydolase activities, that mouse bile or rat cytosol do not contain inhibitors and that freeze-thawing has a significant effect on the activity of epoxide hydolase.

the subcellular distribution of the epoxide hydro-lases in mouse liver is different from that of rat liver, and that the epoxide hy-drolases are stable in subcellular fractions for at least one week when stored at -70°C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model system to study the role of epoxide hydropases in the metabolism of xenobiotic compounds.

the development of a method to prepare subcellular fractions of the liver of C56BL/6 mice, which is suitable for use in studies on epoxide hydrlase isozymes and for other studies requiring subcellular fractions.

the development of an animal model for the study of the role of epoxide hydolases in the metabolism of xenobiotics, and the characterization of the different epoxide hydrlase isozymes present in mouse liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method of preparation and characterization of subfractions from mouse liver is suitable for use in studies on the epoxide hydratase isozymes, as well as in studies on other enzyme activities.
the subcellular distribution of the different enzyme activities in mouse liver is similar to that of rat liver.

a 133,000 x gav for 30 min centrifugation of a 20% homogenate of mouse liver in 1.15% KCl yields a mitochondrial fraction with a specific activity of NADPH-cytochrome P-450 reductase of 1.5 nmol/min/mg protein and a cytosol fraction with a specific glutathione S-transferase activity of 2.5 nmol/mg protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subcellular fractionation procedure described here is suitable for the study of epoxide hydolases and other drug metabolizing enzymes in mouse liver.
the use of 133,000 x g for 60 min, one wash for microsome and two washes of mitochondria, and the use of 0.15 M KCl for cytosol, gave the most pure fractions.

the use of 133,000 x gav for 1 h for cytosolic fractionation, and 105,000 x g for 1 h with one wash for microsome fractionation, and two washes with 105,000 X gav for 30 min for mitochondria fractionation, is recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the subcellular distribution of enzymes in mouse liver closely resemble those reported previously for the rat liver, and that the subcellulat fractions obtained here are suitable for use in studies requiring subcellular fractions of mouse liver.
the use of a 133,000gav for 60 minutes centrifuge step is necessary for the purification of a membrane-free cytoplasmic fraction.
